findings.text: follow-on: the closed-case test exercises only the status "shipped", so a regression that narrows the branch at reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:676 to a single status, or that drops the historical/reference members of TERMINAL_STATUSES, still passes this gate, because no case keys on another terminal status. The membership is read from the owner (reckon/lifecycle.py:9) as intended, but the assertion does not make a narrowed membership redden.

follow-on: the dispatch's done_when asks the gate log to show the closed case failing on the base commit, but gate.log records only the head arm (31 passed, EXIT=0) and its header names revision c5f72a43bba while the run carries the new tests; the base-behaviour failure is demonstrated by negative-control.log, which is a mutated head (terminal short-circuit disabled) rather than a run at the base revision, so the base arm is inferred from the mutation rather than measured at c5f72a43bba.
